content: The medication should be discarded properly when it is expired or no longer needed. The information provided here was last revised in August 2024. Important Usage Information: This document is a summary and does not include all possible details about the product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Possible Side Effects: Common side effects may include stomach upset or pain, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, headache, muscle pain, or diarrhea. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a comprehensive list of side effects. In the U.S.: Contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada: Contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Precautions: Before taking mefloquine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to quinine, or to quinidine, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. This medication may cause dizziness or balance issues. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. Mefloquine may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. Mefloquine passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use (including prescription, non-prescription drugs, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Other medications may affect the removal of mefloquine from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents: Call 1-800-222-1222. Long-Term Use: If you are taking this medication for an extended period, laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g., eye exams, liver function tests) should be conducted regularly. Keep all medical and lab appointments. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store the medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Additional Notes: This information is provided for general informational and educational purposes only. Individual plans may vary, and formulary information is subject to change. Contact the applicable plan provider for the most current information.
